bmt-2025-calculus-tiebreaker-01.title: Cancel the common factor
bmt-2025-calculus-tiebreaker-01.body:
$x^3+1=(x+1)(x^2-x+1)$, so $f(x)=\frac{1}{x^2-x+1}$ for $x\ne-1$ and $\lim_{x\to-1}f(x)=\frac13$.

Solve $\frac1{c^2-c+1}=\frac13$: $c^2-c-2=0$, so $c=2$ or $c=-1$. But $f(-1)$ is undefined, so $c=2$.

**Answer: 2**

bmt-2025-calculus-tiebreaker-03.title: Identify the series
bmt-2025-calculus-tiebreaker-03.body:
$\sin\left(\frac\pi4(2n-1)\right)$ for $n=1,2,3,4,\dots$ is $\frac1{\sqrt2}(+,+,-,-,+,+,\dots)$. Splitting into odd and even $n$:

- odd $n=2i-1$: $\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(x-\frac{x^3}3+\frac{x^5}5-\cdots\right)=\frac1{\sqrt2}\tan^{-1}x$,
- even $n=2j$: $\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(\frac{x^2}2-\frac{x^4}4+\cdots\right)=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\ln(1+x^2)$.

So the integral is $\frac1{\sqrt2}\int_0^1\left(\tan^{-1}x+\frac12\ln(1+x^2)\right)dx$. Using $\int_0^1\tan^{-1}x\,dx=\frac\pi4-\frac12\ln2$ and $\int_0^1\ln(1+x^2)dx=\ln2-2+\frac\pi2$:
$$\frac1{\sqrt2}\left(\frac\pi4-\frac12\ln2+\frac12\ln2-1+\frac\pi4\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\left(\frac\pi2-1\right)=\frac{\pi-2}{2\sqrt2}.$$

**Answer: $\frac{\pi-2}{2\sqrt2}$**
